blocks.text: בִּרְכוֹת אַחֲרוֹנוֹת לְהַפְטָרָה
uncertainties: The page number 80 is printed at both the left and right corners of the header.

blocks.text: מְרִיבָו֯ עָלָו֯ בַּשָּׁמַיִם יַרְעֵם יְהוָה יָדִין אַפְסֵי־אָרֶץ וְיִתֶּן־עֹז לְמַלְכּוֹ וְיָרֵם קֶרֶן מְשִׁיחוֹ׃
uncertainties: This verse continues from the previous page. The page starts mid-verse at מְרִיבָו, and the earlier part of the verse is not on this page.

Small reference marks sit above מְרִיבָו (a circle °) and above עָלָו (an asterisk-like mark over the ע, plus a small mark near the ו). They point to the qere footnote. The ֯ in my text only stands in for these marks. Their exact placement is uncertain.

A few marks that look like accents appear in the large Haftarah type. There is a small mark above בַּשָּׁמַיִם (over the מ), one above יַרְעֵם, one above יְהוָה, and sublinear marks under יָדִין, אָרֶץ (possibly etnachta under the א), וְיִתֶּן, לְמַלְכּוֹ (mark above the כ), וְיָרֵם, קֶרֶן and מְשִׁיחוֹ (possibly a silluq/meteg under the ח). I could not identify them reliably at this resolution, so I left them out instead of filling them in from memory. They need checking against the original.
אַפְסֵי־ ends line 1 with a maqaf, and אָרֶץ starts line 2. Joined here.

blocks.text: °) ביו ק׳. — *) ליו ק׳.
uncertainties: Small footnote under the verse. ° refers to מריבו (qere מריביו), and * refers to עלו (qere עליו).

blocks.text: המפטיר יברך ברכות אחרונות.
uncertainties: Printed in small Rashi script, unpointed.

blocks.text: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם צוּר כָּל־הָעוֹלָמִים צַדִּיק בְּכָל־הַדּוֹרוֹת הָאֵל הַנֶּאֱמָן הָאוֹמֵר וְעוֹשֶׂה הַמְדַבֵּר וּמְקַיֵּם שֶׁכָּל־דְּבָרָיו אֱמֶת וָצֶדֶק׃
uncertainties: A meteg may be present in הָעוֹלָמִים. It is not clearly visible.

blocks.text: נֶאֱמָן אַתָּה הוּא יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וְנֶאֱמָנִים דְּבָרֶיךָ וְדָבָר אֶחָד מִדְּבָרֶיךָ אָחוֹר לֹא־יָשׁוּב רֵיקָם כִּי אֵל מֶלֶךְ נֶאֱמָן וְרַחֲמָן אָתָּה. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ הָאֵל הַנֶּאֱמָן בְּכָל־דְּבָרָיו׃
uncertainties: The final אָתָּה (pausal form with qamats) may have a meteg under the א. This is uncertain.

blocks.text: רַחֵם עַל־צִיּוֹן כִּי הִיא בֵּית חַיֵּינוּ וְלַעֲלוּבַת נֶפֶשׁ תּוֹשִׁיעַ בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ מְשַׂמֵּחַ צִיּוֹן בְּבָנֶיהָ׃
uncertainties: I cannot tell whether the ב of בְיָמֵינוּ has a dagesh. It looks rafe/undotted, but this is uncertain.
The dagesh in the ת of תּוֹשִׁיעַ is faint.

blocks.text: שַׂמְּחֵנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ בְּאֵלִיָּהוּ הַנָּבִיא עַבְדֶּךָ וּבְמַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד מְשִׁיחֶךָ בִּמְהֵרָה יָבֹא וְיָגֵל לִבֵּנוּ. עַל־כִּסְאוֹ לֹא־יֵשֶׁב זָר וְלֹא יִנְחֲלוּ עוֹד אֲחֵרִים אֶת־כְּבוֹדוֹ. כִּי בְשֵׁם קָדְשְׁךָ נִשְׁבַּעְתָּ לּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא־יִכְבֶּה נֵרוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ מָגֵן דָּוִד׃
uncertainties: דָּוִד is spelled defectively (without yod) both times, as printed.
I cannot tell whether the ב of בְשֵׁם has a dagesh.
I cannot tell whether the ל of לּוֹ has a dagesh (dagesh forte conjunctive). It may be undotted.
The final line 'בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ מָגֵן דָּוִד׃' is set on its own line.

blocks.text: עַל־הַתּוֹרָה וְעַל־הָעֲבוֹדָה וְעַל־הַנְּבִיאִים וְעַל־יוֹם (הַשַּׁבָּת הַזֶּה וְיוֹם) הַזִּכָּרוֹן הַזֶּה שֶׁנָּתַתָּ לָּנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ (לִקְדֻשָּׁה וְלִמְנוּחָה) לְכָבוֹד וּלְתִפְאָרֶת. עַל־הַכֹּל יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ אֲנַחְנוּ מוֹדִים לָךְ וּמְבָרְכִים אוֹתָךְ. יִתְבָּרַךְ שִׁמְךָ בְּפִי כָּל־חַי תָּמִיד לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד. וּדְבָרְךָ אֱמֶת וְקַיָּם לָעַד׃ בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ מֶלֶךְ עַל כָּל הָאָרֶץ מְקַדֵּשׁ (הַשַּׁבָּת וְ) יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיוֹם הַזִּכָּרוֹן׃
uncertainties: The Sabbath additions in parentheses are printed in smaller type.
וּמְבָרְכִים אוֹתָךְ is set very tightly and almost runs together. I treat it as two words.
In 'עַל כָּל הָאָרֶץ' I see no maqaf.
In '(הַשַּׁבָּת וְ)' the וְ is inside the parenthesis, as printed.
I cannot tell whether the ל of לָּנוּ has a dagesh.

blocks.text: On Sabbath the following passages are omitted and the Service continues with יקום פרקן (p. 85).
uncertainties: Italic English rubric printed on the Hebrew page.

blocks.text: יקום פרקן
uncertainties: Hebrew linkage words inside the English rubric. Printed defectively as פרקן, without vav.

blocks.text: Benedictions following the Haphtorah
uncertainties: The page number 80 is printed at both corners.

blocks.text: man prevails. As for the Lord, His opponents will be crushed, in heaven above does He thunder, the Lord will judge the ends of the earth and give strength to His king and raise the condition of his anointed.
uncertainties: The page starts mid-sentence. 'man prevails' completes 2:9 from the previous page.

blocks.text: Blessings after the Haphtorah:
ברוך
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, Rock of all eternity, just in all generations, faithful God who says and acts, speaks and fulfils, for all His words are truth and righteousness.
נאמן

Faithful art Thou, O Lord our God and faithful are Thy words and not one of Thy words turns back empty; for Thou art a faithful and compassionate God and King. Blessed art Thou, O Lord God who is faithful in all His words.
רחם
Have mercy upon Zion, it is the centre of our life; and save her, whose soul is afflicted, speedily in our days. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, who makes Zion rejoice with her children.
שמחנו

Let us rejoice, O Lord our God, with the prophet Elijah Thy servant and with the realm of the House of David thine anointed. Speedily may he come that our heart may have joy. Let no stranger sit on his throne, and let others no longer inherit his glory for by Thy Holy Name hast Thou sworn to him that his light shall not be extinguished for ever. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, shield of David.
uncertainties: 'thine' is lowercase as printed. There is no comma after 'glory'.

blocks.text: על התורה

For the Torah, for the service of God, for the prophets and for this (Sabbath day and this) day of memorial, which Thou, O Lord our God, hast given us, (for holiness and rest) for honour and glory, for all these, O Lord our God, do we thank Thee and bless Thee. Blessed be Thy name in the mouth of all the living constantly and for ever and ever, Thy word is truth and endures to eternity. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, King over all the earth who sanctifies (the Sabbath) Israel and the day of memorial.
After the Haphtora the Shofar is blown. But when the first day of the festival falls on a Sabbath, then one continues immediately with יקום פורקן (p. 85)
uncertainties: Italic. Printed as 'Haphtora', without a final h, which differs from 'Haphtorah' elsewhere. No final period after (p. 85).

blocks.text: יקום פורקן
uncertainties: Printed here plene as פורקן, while the Hebrew page s182 has פרקן.

notes: I read both pages independently from the full scans and all enlarged bands. Where bands overlapped, the shared lines appear only once.
s182 is the end of 1 Samuel 2:10, which continues from the previous page, followed by the blessings after the Haftarah. There is no chapter or aliyah label on this page.
There are qere/ketiv footnotes for מריבו (qere מריביו) and עלו (qere עליו), marked with ° and *.

The Haftarah type has some scattered accent-like marks (see the uncertainties on s182_haftarah_verse_cont). I did not add any cantillation from memory. A possible etnachta under אָרֶץ and a possible silluq under מְשִׁיחוֹ are the most likely ones, but neither is confirmed.
There is a spelling difference between the pages: the Hebrew-page rubric has יקום פרקן and the English page has יקום פורקן.

The two Sabbath rubrics differ in wording. The Hebrew page says the following passages are omitted on Sabbath. The English page says the Shofar is blown after the Haftarah unless the first day falls on a Sabbath.
